key_insight: Certain non-unital noise, when combined with universal gates, can accelerate the emergence of Haar-like output states by acting like an effective expansion on the pure-state manifold.
engineering_relevance: This suggests noise may be harnessed as a controllable resource in quantum algorithms and reservoir-style processors, potentially improving state mixing and performance in some regimes.
method: Built a minimal 1-qubit model using amplitude damping plus a renormalization rule that maps mixed states back to representative pure states.
Analyzed the induced nonlinear map on pure states and derived the local area expansion factor and global expansion threshold.
Tested the idea with the universal gate set G3 = {H, T, CNOT} to study mixing toward Haar-like behavior.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports an analytical derivation of expansion conditions and shows that, in an appropriate parameter region, amplitude damping plus G3 leads to faster convergence toward Haar-like distributions.
watch_item: The effect relies on a specific non-unital noise channel and a renormalization scheme, so the advantage may be regime-dependent and not directly transferable to all hardware noise models.
paper_title: On the question of noise as a resource in quantum computing
